web.named_query: ("William Kimmitt" OR "Department of Commerce") AI artificial intelligence superintelligence policy statements

summary.text: On April 27, 2026, Kimmitt described AI adoption as a source of productivity, stronger public services, and future growth, calling it a historic opportunity for developing countries. He said realizing those benefits would require infrastructure, energy, training, trusted vendors, and frameworks that encourage innovation while protecting security. On June 18, 2026, he described Commerce's implementation of the American AI Exports Program and its effort to promote American AI capabilities abroad.

We’re bringing together industry-led consortia that can offer the full range of American AI capabilities: semiconductors, servers, data centers, cloud infrastructure, models, cybersecurity, software, and real-world applications. Approved consortia under this program will benefit from America’s commercial, diplomatic, advocacy, and financing tools for major projects abroad. We want countries choosing American chips, American infrastructure, American software, American standards, and American expertise.
